evidence: Etymonline: "from Old English foda 'food, nourishment; fuel,' from PIE *pat-, extended form of root *pa- 'to feed'"
Wiktionary: "cognate with Latin pānis 'bread, food,' pāscō 'feed, nourish'; related to fodder, foster"
food.mechanism_sentence: 从Old English到今天，核心意思一直是「食物」，没有大变化，是直接传下来的老词。

semantic_path.how: 所指没变，它的根 *pa- 是『喂』：喂人的东西在拉丁语里长成了 pānis（面包），在英语里 food 守住总称，亲戚 fodder 分去管牲口的饲料。

chain_flags: source_chain 的印欧语两站（*ḱers-『跑』、*ḱr̥sós『车辆』）及原始日耳曼语站把未定论的谱系写成了定局编年：Etymonline 对原始日耳曼语 *harss- 明言『of unknown origin』，『跑』说、『车辆』说与伊朗语借词说并存。建议链上标注『推测谱系』，路径改以古英语 hors『马』为首站。
changes: original_meaning 由印欧词根 *ḱers- 的 gloss『跑』改为最早历史词古英语 hors 的义『马』（『跑→车辆→马』的编年是推测谱系，不是见载编年，原稿写成了定局）
semantic_path 重建两站：马→马形支架（14世纪晚期起）

evidence: Etymonline: "Old English hors 'horse,' from Proto-Germanic *harss-, of unknown origin. By some, connected to PIE root *kers- 'to run'... Boutkan prefers the theory that it is a loan-word from an Iranian language (Sarmatian)"; "The usual Indo-European word is represented by Old English eoh, Greek hippos, Latin equus, from PIE root *ekwo-. In many languages the PIE root has been lost in favor of synonyms, probably via superstitious taboo"; "Used at least since late 14c. of various devices or appliances which suggest a horse"
Wiktionary: "from Proto-Germanic *hrussą 'horse,' most likely from PIE *ḱr̥sós 'vehicle,' from *ḱers- 'to run'"
horse.mechanism_sentence: horse 的身世至今没定论：通行词源说日耳曼语的这个词『来源不明』——一说连着『跑』的词根，一说它的源头本指『车辆』，还有学者主张它借自伊朗语。能确定的是，印欧语本来的马词 *ekwo-（希腊语 hippos、拉丁语 equus）在英语里丢了，替换它的多半是忌讳：太重要的动物，人们不敢直呼其名。

semantic_path.how: 凡是跨着站、驮着东西的架子都像一匹马：锯木头的 sawhorse 就这么得名（以驮载的姿态借名，比喻）。
